items.text: eNOAD dysfunctional/critical equipment reporting (33 CFR 164) — All defective machinery must be reported to USCG via eNOA; revised eNOA without delay if found after submission. M/E and G/E normal operation confirmed before US call (USCG focus area; USD 150K fine imposed on a managed vessel in 2024). Deviation letter required via local agent.

Garbage handling (CBP penalty) — Garbage must be kept in tight, covered, leak-proof receptacles per 33 CFR 94.5. Avoid large bags; if unavoidable, keep tied in deck store and plan discharge at upcoming ports.
HAZMAT CBT training — Vessels calling USA require IMDG CBT (No.0053 Basic / No.0151 Advanced) for all crew, 3-year interval, printed records kept onboard.

Ballast water / VGP / BWTS — With overdue BWTS extension letter or AMS-BWTS, ocean exchange is NOT allowed (heavy fines). VGP and BFMP to be maintained per Docmap US documentation; Ballast Water Logbook per Circular 025-19.

RACE drill & response plans — RACE drill compliance per CFR (one fleet vessel per 3 years); NTVRP & CANTVCP to be kept updated; QI notification drill required — any serious accident in USA/Canada reported to QI.

US port security advisory — Vessels that visited countries listed in the USCG Port Security Advisory during their last five port calls must take prescribed actions 1-5 as a condition of entry into US ports.
CBP visa penalty — Approx. USD 6,000 per person imposed when crew without valid US visa go out via stern ramp. Strict access control required.
Bunkering & NOA — Annual hydrostatic testing of bunker lines per CFR 156. Do NOT sign bunkering agreements indemnifying the barge under OPA. Fuel type must be indicated on NOA per USCG MSIB-11-23.

EEXI / EPL (USCG Policy Letter 01-24) — Pilot Card updated with original/limited RPM & power; override & recording procedure posted at bridge and ECR consoles; officers familiarized; report to Class/OCMI if override activated.
AGM certification — USA is an AGM country (with Canada, Chile, Argentina, Australia, NZ); crew pre-inspection and AGM certificate obtained before departure from Asia.
VHF four-digit channel numbers — Per MSIB 07-24, new VHF radios show four-digit channels (22A is now 1022). USCG broadcasts UMIB on 1022; bridge-to-bridge must be capable of 22A (157.1 MHz).
Ship Sanitation Certificates — Per USCG MSIB 005/2017, SSCC/SSCEC not normally required for commercial ships in US ports; only CDC may issue.

Vessel Vetting Form & Pre-Berthing Checklist — From 01 May 2026 all vessels must complete a Vessel Vetting Form (every voyage non-regular; every 90 days regular) and a Pre-Berthing Checklist (24-48h before arrival).

Salvage Response Plan & ship salvage preparedness — Pilbara Ports introduced the Port Hedland Salvage Response Plan (PH-SRP). From 01 Aug 2026 vessels >120,000 DWT must have a Port Hedland Ship Salvage Plan aligned with PH-SRP.

Requirements for dual/alternative-fuel vessels — Pre-arrival (>=14 days): submit vessel details/plans, fuel system info, HAZID/HAZOP, crew competency, photos. In port: switch to LSFO/MGO; alternative fuel needs Harbour Master approval.

Aux engine/emergency gen/steering gear requirements (Capesize >=120,000 DWT) — Due to single-entry shallow channel, power failures risk grounding; Capesize must ensure aux engines, emergency generator, steering gear comply and are maintained.

Seawater strainer blockage from jellyfish — Increased jellyfish causing strainer accumulation and reduced seawater flow - risks to ME/aux cooling, ballast ops, fire pumps, crew. Increase inspection; use PPE.
Annual dredging maintenance — Maintenance dredging from 12 Sep 2025 for 3-4 weeks across inner harbour, channel, adjacent areas, spoil grounds. Dredgers monitor VHF 12/16.
CCTV requirement for Capesize — From 01 Jan 2025 all Capesize (>120,000 DWT) must fit >=1 CCTV rudder camera in steering gear flat with a wheelhouse monitor; verified by pilots.
Emergency steering preparedness — Notice 19/24: competent personnel in steering gear room during inbound/outbound; Capesize departure tests must verify emergency steering and rudder control.
CCTV in steering gear flat (Capesize) — From 01 Jan 2025 (MSB 02/2024) all Capesize (>=120,000 DWT) must fit >=1 CCTV camera on/in front of rudder with a wheelhouse monitor.
Mooring standards implementation — From 01 Jan 2025 ship-specific Mooring Line Management Plan: lines max 110mm/min 220m; tails 11-22m; min 4 spare lines + 4 tails.
Chafe protection on mooring lines — Evaluations raised concerns that chafe protection introduces crew-safety risks and operational delays; recommendations to discontinue.
Attempted robbery — Perpetrators with knives threatened the crew of a bulk carrier underway in the Singapore Strait; escaped on crew response. Crew safe.
Armed robbery (LNG tanker) — Two intruders with swords boarded an LNG tanker; spotted in engine room, ran to poop deck and escaped. Some auxiliary engine spares missing.
Robbery (bulk carrier) — Padlock to engine room found broken on a bulk carrier; search found no perpetrators. Some engine spares and fire hydrant nozzles stolen.

Robbery / armed robbery x2 (EB lane) — Incident 1: 10 robbers from 9 sampans boarded a barge under tow, removed scrap metal. Incident 2: 3 unarmed perpetrators in engine room fled; PCG boarded, none found.

Robbery / armed robbery x4 (EB lane) — Four incidents: broken padlocks (deck store, steering gear, engine casing); engine stores/spares stolen; in one, armed perpetrators boarded via chock liner and fled.
Armed robbery x6 (EB lane) — Six incidents on tankers/bulk/cargo ships: perpetrators (knives, gun-like objects) in engine rooms; spares, lube oil, paint drums stolen; one crew minor head injury.
Robbery (EB lane TSS) — Robbers boarded a bulk carrier unnoticed; footprints found, steering gear room lock broken. Generator spares stolen.

Armed robbery x3 (TSS) — Incident 1: 4 perpetrators locked up a duty oiler, escaped with spares. Incident 2: via steering gear room injured a crew member; vessel diverted. Incident 3: 6-7 armed, no theft.
Armed robbery x3 (EB lane) — Three incidents on bulk carriers: robbers (knives/gun-like objects) in engine rooms; one Chief Engineer tied up and engine spares stolen.
Attempted robbery / robbery x2 — Incident 1: five robbers on a sampan hooked a ladder to a tanker (WB lane), aborted on alarm. Incident 2: four robbers boarded a tanker (EB lane), nothing stolen.

Robbery x2 (anchorage) — Incident 1: sea robbers boarded via anchor chain, broke into forecastle bosun's store, jumped overboard when noticed. Incident 2: two robbers escaped with cans of paint after alarm.

Robbery x2 (anchorage) — Incident 1: sea robbers boarded via anchor chain, broke into forecastle bosun's store, jumped overboard when noticed. Incident 2: two robbers escaped with cans of paint after alarm.
Attempted boarding (anchorage) — A container vessel boarded by one person via poop deck; patrol boat dispatched, hanging rope found at stern and removed. Search confirmed no intruder; crew safe.
Robbery (anchorage) — A vessel boarded undetected; crew later noticed items stolen. CCTV revealed four perpetrators had boarded. Crew safe.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — Two robbers spotted on a tanker at anchorage; fled to a waiting boat on alarm. Nothing stolen.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Three robbers with knives boarded an anchored bulk carrier near the forecastle; escaped with ship's property when a patrol boat approached.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — Unknown number of perpetrators boarded an anchored bulk carrier near hold 1; escaped empty-handed on alarm.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Three perpetrators with long knives boarded an anchored bulk carrier, threatened crew and escaped; paint locker broken into and stores stolen.
Robbery (anchorage) — Two robbers spotted on main deck of an anchored cargo vessel; escaped on alarm. Search confirmed ship's property stolen.

Usage of e-vaporisers (stepped-up enforcement) — MPA circular: stepped-up enforcement vs e-vaporisers (esp. etomidate). Higher penalties/rehabilitation; foreigners' devices seized with NOC; repeat offenders banned/deported.

Maritime Declaration of Health (Nipah Virus) — MPA/NEA require MDH (Annex B) >=12h before arrival to prevent Nipah Virus, with crew list, Ship Sanitation Certificate, last 10 ports, list of anyone with temp >37.5C. Source MPA PMC 02/2026.
Increased penalties for e-vaporisers — From 01 Sep 2025 stricter penalties for possessing/using/buying e-vaporisers: confiscation, fines, re-entry bans, deportation; harsher if containing etomidate.
Immigration clearance for arriving sea crew — ICA reminder: IPL crew present for clearance with valid docs and SG Arrival Card; NTL crew remain onboard unless uplifted. Source MPA PMN 46/2025.
Maritime Declaration of Health (Mpox) — From 04 Sep 2024 MPA requires MDH submitted to NEA Port Health Office >=12h before arrival if ship called at Mpox-affected countries within 21 days.
Health screening for Mpox — After WHO declared Mpox a PHEIC (14 Aug 2024), Singapore implements screening at sea checkpoints for crew/passengers from affected areas.
Just-in-Time (JIT) Arrival implementation — From Jan 2024 JIT Platform applies to tankers at energy terminals and all vessels at anchorages; MPA notifies berth 72h before arrival.

Theft x2 — Incident 1: sea robbers boarded a bulk carrier berthed at Eko Terminal from the riverside, stole paint cans, escaped on a canoe. Incident 2: eight people in two skiffs stole paint boxes and thinner.
Robbery (alongside) — A bulk carrier boarded alongside Eko Terminal; perpetrators boarded from the riverside and stole a quantity of paint. Crew safe.
Robbery (anchorage) — Three perpetrators near paint locker of a tanker; alarm raised, crew mustered. Absconded with ship stores; no injuries.
Robbery (anchorage) — A tanker boarded by four suspects; escaped empty-handed when spotted. Crew/vessel safe; reported to port authorities.
Robbery (berth) — Storeroom of a general cargo ship berthed at Lagos found broken into; ship stores/property stolen. Reported to agent.
Robbery (berth) — Four unauthorized persons boarded a tanker berthed at Lagos; escaped when spotted. Reported to port authorities.
Robbery (berth) — Robbers accessed ship's stores on a cargo ship berthed at Lagos and stole a quantity of paint boxes.
Robbery (anchorage) — Seven perpetrators boarded an LPG tanker; watchman saw them attempting to enter the bosun store, raised alarm; they escaped empty-handed.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Eight robbers with knives boarded a container ship, stole stores and escaped. Coast Guard investigated; crew safe.
Robbery (anchorage) — Five robbers from a wooden boat boarded a general cargo ship and stole ~30 cans of paint; anti-smuggling team apprehended them and returned property.
Robbery (night watch) — 6-7 robbers from a wooden boat boarded, attacked the watchman with a machete and took his radio/phone and accessible items; disembarked on general alarm.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Two perpetrators on main deck of a container ship chased a crew member; robbers escaped. Considerable stores and paint stolen.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — Two persons on a small boat prepared to throw a grappling hook at an anchored tanker; abandoned on alarm and fire hoses.

Armed robbery x2 (anchorage) — Incident 1: two armed intruders via anchor hawse pipe; crew in citadel, perpetrators left on alarm. Incident 2: one perpetrator with knife climbed anchor chain; escaped, equipment stolen.

Armed robbery x2 (anchorage) — Incident 1: two armed intruders via anchor hawse pipe; crew in citadel, perpetrators left on alarm. Incident 2: one perpetrator with knife climbed anchor chain; escaped, equipment stolen.
Robbery (outer anchorage) — Robbers boarded a tanker at Luanda outer anchorage; forecastle storeroom broken into and ship property stolen.
Robbery (decoy) — Persons posing as vendors diverted crew while robbers boarded the opposite side; escaped with lifeboat outboard engine.
Robbery (anchorage) — Robbers boarded an anchored vessel unseen and stole two mooring lines; discovered later during routine rounds.
Robbery x2 (anchorage) — Incident 1: two 50m mooring ropes stolen from a supply vessel. Incident 2: five robbers overpowered a crew member; escaped on alarm.

PCSOPEP — Plan approval required (submit 96h before; USD 2,000 penalty for non-compliance); Authorized-Person notification exercise twice per year documented for ACP verification. Minimum transit draft and Panama light fuel to be reviewed.

Transit equipment requirements — Wheelhouse/pilot A/C must hold 21-26 C and 40-70% RH or disruption charge applies (OP Notice N-1-2023 s.24). Green Vessel Classification: IEEC/EEDI, bow-thruster/displacement ratio and BDN submitted. NPU/PPU fixed RTK antenna procedure applies.

New risk-based vessel inspection model — From 01 Oct 2025 all vessels undergo initial physical inspection valid one year; subsequent visits may qualify for digital inspection. Mandatory from 01 Jan 2026.
Increase in maximum authorized draft (49 ft) — From 16 Aug 2024 max draft 15.24 m (49 ft) TFW; more transit slots expected to reduce waiting (Advisory A-28-2024).
Increase in maximum authorized draft — From 27 Jun 2024 max draft for Neopanamax locks 14.33 m (47 ft); from 11 Jul 2024 14.63 m (48 ft) per Advisory A-20-2024.
Maximum permitted drafts increase — From 15 Jun 2024 max draft for Neopanamax locks increased to 13.71 m (45 ft) from 13.41 m (44 ft).

Foreign vessels entering territorial waters in emergency — PRC MSA rules for foreign-flagged vessels entering Chinese waters in emergencies without permit; ensure AIS/VHF, report via 12395 hotline; submit Emergency Report Form.
Proper flying of national flag — Vessels punished for improperly flying the PRC flag. Foreign ships fly it daily; flag class A-E by ship length; not smaller than flag-state flag.
Enclosed space entry inspection campaign — China MSA special campaign 15 Jan-14 Oct 2025: crew training, permit-to-work, atmosphere testing/rescue equipment, enclosed space drills.

One-time vessel position reporting — PRC MSA requires vessels >=80 m (excl. passenger/trial) to report AIS info when transiting designated waters (Bohai Rim; Yangtze; Pearl River Delta; Qiongzhou; Beibu Gulf).
Administrative penalties by maritime authorities — Rise in penalties for violating rules; drones monitor ships. Common: illegal discharge of sewage/food waste/cargo residues.
Shore power usage requirements — Penalties for vessels with shore-power capability that fail to use it; non-tankers >3h coastal / >2h inland equipped berths; cruise >3h.
Armed robbery — A bulk carrier boarded in the EB lane TSS off Pulau Nongsa/Cula; perpetrators with knives in steering gear room, some engine spares stolen. Crew safe; reported to Singapore VTIS.
Robbery / armed robbery — Bulk carrier underway ~7.3 nm off Pulau Cula; two perpetrators with knives entered the engine room and stole engine spares.
Armed robbery x2 (EB lane) — Two incidents on bulk carriers off Pulau Cula: engine/generator spares and personal belongings stolen; crew safe.
Armed robbery x4 — Knife/gun-armed robbers boarded bulk carriers/tanker in EB lane, escaping with engine spares; one piracy incident saw 20 perpetrators take scrap metal from a towed barge.
Robbery (EB lane) — Four unarmed perpetrators boarded a bulk carrier underway in EB lane TSS; spotted in engine room, escaped empty-handed.
Attempted robbery (EB lane) — One perpetrator with a gun-like object boarded a bulk carrier in EB lane; escaped when discovered on upper deck. Nothing stolen.
Armed robbery x2 — Two incidents on bulk carriers transiting the channel; 4 perpetrators each entered machinery spaces. Nothing stolen in one, ship's parts stolen in the other.
Attempted robbery — Two perpetrators reportedly with knives found in engine room of a tanker transiting EB lane of Phillip Channel. Crew/vessel safe, nothing stolen; continued to Vietnam.

Boarded robbery (tanker) — Chief Engineer encountered armed intruders in engine-room workshop; they threatened duty crew with machetes/metal rods before absconding. VTIS West informed; engine spares stolen.
Robbery x3 — Three incidents on bulk carriers underway: robbers (some with metal rods) in engine rooms; escaped with engine parts in two, nothing stolen in one.
Robbery x2 — Incident 1: six robbers with knives tied up engine crew, escaped with spares. Incident 2: four robbers with gun-like objects, parts missing.
Theft — A vessel boarded by one person at Abidjan; alarm raised when a small boat and an individual on deck were seen. Individual jumped overboard. Nothing stolen; crew safe.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Four perpetrators with knives boarded a supply vessel; alarm raised when seen. Escaped after stealing a fast rescue craft and paint cans. Crew safe.
Robbery (attempted) — A perpetrator attempted to board via anchor chain at Abidjan anchorage; escaped on alarm.
Robbery — A robber with a knife boarded an anchored vessel, stole a phone and escaped.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — Two robbers boarded an anchored offshore supply vessel; spotted on starboard main deck. Paint store lock broken and paint stolen.
Robbery (anchorage) — Robbers boarded a bulk carrier at Callao and stole the ship's forward mooring ropes before escaping. Crew safe.
Robbery (anchorage) — Robbers boarded a bulk carrier at Callao and stole the ship's forward mooring ropes before escaping.
Robbery (anchorage) — Five robbers with knives boarded an anchored tanker via anchor chain, threatened a crew member, forced into the forecastle store and escaped.
Robbery (anchorage) — Ten robbers with knives boarded an anchored bulk carrier and restrained a crew member; escaped with crew belongings and ship stores.
Enhanced marine pollution fines — Fines by GT not spill volume, up ~44% from 01 Jan 2025. Multipliers: hazardous x10, protection zone x2, corporate x3 - most ocean-going vessels >=6x base, up to 60x.
Environmental pollution fines increased — Revised tariff from 01 Jan 2025, up 43.9% vs 2024, by vessel tonnage; multipliers for repeat/hazardous/corporate; 25% early-payment discount.
Bunker oil declaration accuracy — Customs require accurate bunker declaration on arrival; over-declaration may lead to confiscation, deposit and criminal prosecution.
Bunker declaration before entering port — Customs randomly inspect for discrepancies between declared and measured bunkers; excess may be treated as smuggling.
UAV attack — A UAV strike caused a fire at the Fujairah Oil Industries Zone; three people injured.
Kinetic attack — A tanker hit by falling debris from an intercepted weapon while at anchor off Fujairah; minor structural damage, crew unharmed.
Ship Sanitation Certificates reinstated — Fujairah accepts only SSCC/SSCEC issued by institutions registered under the IHR Authorized Port List.
Robbery (anchorage) — Three unknown persons spotted aboard a vessel during rounds (port-side midship locker and forecastle). Armed guards informed Togo Navy; no harm.
Suspicious approach — A small craft with seven persons circled a cargo vessel at anchor at night; fled when floodlit; returned ~24h later and came alongside, departing when illuminated.
Enhanced risk of customs penalties — Ships detained until fines settled after sludge/scrap/water exchanged for sim cards/seafood; treated as smuggling.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Ten perpetrators with knives and bats attacked an anchored bulk carrier; crew assaulted, ship property and stores stolen.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Eight robbers with knives boarded a bulk carrier; alarm raised, robbers escaped with ship's stores.
Robbery (anchorage) — Nine robbers boarded an anchored LNG tanker, tied up the watchman and escaped with stores; all nine later apprehended.

Discontinuation of DGPS correction service — Marine Dept will discontinue its DGPS correction service from 01 Jan 2027 (GNSS accuracy now sufficient); use alternative DGNSS stations (IALA list). Source Notice 16/2026.
DGPS correction service temporarily out of service — HO Marine Dept DGPS service suspended for maintenance until further notice; use alternative DGNSS stations (IALA list).
Reduced speed in restricted zones — 5-knot limits 0800-2400 in restricted zones (Port Shelter/Rocky Harbor K3 daily; HK Island South, Lamma, Cheung Chau, Lantau, Tolo Harbor).
Navigation/reporting near whales — Humpback migration through Dampier waters Jun-Nov raises collision risk. Maintain 100m either side / 300m front-behind; watch VHF 11/16.
Bridge wing shelters — From 01 Sep 2024 mandatory for bulk/cargo >=81,000 DWT and gas tankers >=60,000 m3 (>=1.52m inboard, >=2.45m height, weatherproof, unrestricted visibility).
Hatch cover operation — Foldable hatches must be fully open or closed unless fitted with manufacturer-approved tent-position devices, and once open fastened before power off.
Robbery (anchorage) — 6-7 perpetrators boarded an anchored container ship by ladder; few lashing gears stolen, no injuries. Marine Police boarded; ICG alerted.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — Three robbers spotted boarding an anchored vessel off Kandla; escaped empty-handed on alarm.
Robbery (anchorage) — Cargo equipment found missing from an anchored tanker; CCTV revealed five robbers had boarded and stolen it.

Revised biofouling regulations — From 10 Jun 2026 Brazil fully enforces mandatory biofouling regs (NORMAM-401/DPC) for commercial vessels >24m. Visible growth (Level 2+) not permitted. Fines up to BRL 50m.
Biofouling updates — From 17 Jun 2025 reactive hull cleaning where increased biofouling found; full enforcement with penalties 01 Feb 2026. Ships >24m need Plan, Record Book, protocols.
Ballast water management inspections — Per NORMAM 20, Brazilian Navy/Coast Guard inspect BWM Plan, Record Book, reporting and compliance.
Integrated waste management — From 14 May 2025 SCA + ANTIPOLLUTION EGYPT launch solid-waste collection for all vessels in Suez Canal waters; mandatory fees by Net Tonnage, charged even if unused.
Shore-based mooring services — From 01 May 2024 mooring mainly shore-based; ~30% of ships still need onboard boats; fines for refusing.
Armed robbery — Fourteen robbers boarded a laid-up general cargo ship from a fishing trawler, subdued seven crew and looted fuel oil, supplies, equipment, phones. Some crew injured.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Eight robbers with knives boarded a tanker; horn sounded, robbers escaped with ship's stores.
Armed robbery (berthing) — Up to twenty robbers with knives boarded a vessel berthing at Tincan, restrained crew/stevedore/bosun, stole cargo from containers and escaped on two skiffs.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — Robbers discovered by duty crew at Tin Can Island; one crew member injured as robbers escaped.

Korea ECA & domestic requirements — 0.1%S fuel at Incheon, Pyeongtaek-Dangjin, Yeosu-Gwangyang, Busan and Ulsan (from 1h after berthing/anchoring until 1h before departure). While drifting, engine kept ready and proper lights shown. VHF recording (Korea flag/BBCHP), KCG inspections, MLC complaint procedure displayed, ballast reporting to agent.
Pilot ladder safety management — Vessels must install/manage pilot boarding facilities per Pilot Act and SOLAS; 25 of 46 accidents (2013-2023) were falls due to poor facilities.
Supply of mooring ropes — Haldia Dock Complex approved returnable-basis supply of mooring ropes; request by the berthing meeting. Inspect rented ropes before use.
Robbery (berth) — Several perpetrators accessed a berthed bulk carrier and escaped with engine spares. Crew safe.

Freshwater analysis & wastewater — Arrange freshwater analysis (galley, purifier, cabins; 3-6 month interval) before arrival. Port guidelines on vessel wastewater and in-water hull cleaning to be reviewed.
Stowaway — A male stowaway (claimed Afghan, ~22) climbed the terminal fence, hid in a Canada-bound vehicle, found ~24h after departure; handed over at Halifax.
Attempted robbery — Five perpetrators with metal rods boarded a tanker in EB lane; escaped when discovered in engine room. Nothing stolen.
Robbery / attempted robbery (several) — Several incidents on bulk carriers underway in EB lane; robbers spotted in engine rooms. Engine spare parts found missing.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Two perpetrators with knives boarded a tanker; escaped when spotted. Nothing stolen.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — One perpetrator attempted to board an anchored LPG tanker; four more in a boat near the anchor chain; escaped on fire pumps.

Ballast water regulation reinstated — Santos reinstated Ballast Water Regulation via court injunction; vessels must present BWM Certificate, approved Plan, Form B, BWTS producer certification; third-party verification required.
Ballast water compliance requirement (suspended) — Santos introduced (21 Aug) a compliance-statement requirement; suspended from 09 Sep after complaints.
Kidnapping — Armed individuals boarded a bulk carrier drifting ~6 NM west of Port-au-Prince and kidnapped two crew before fleeing.
Civil unrest impacting port — On 26 Sep a crane operator was shot during operations at the APN port; terminal shut down. Vessels advised to hold 20-25 NM off, berth in daylight with escort.
Biofouling updates — From 01 Jul 2028 ships with fouling must clean within 24h; cleaning risking pollution/spread of non-native species not done in Norwegian waters; removed fouling sent ashore.
High risk of flying drones — Strict Norwegian drone laws; non-compliance risks fines, arrest or deportation. Keep drones <120m, line of sight, away from restricted areas.
Robbery (offshore) — A robbery aboard a multipurpose offshore vessel near Pemex Maritime Terminal; ~6 armed perpetrators boarded and made verbal threats. No damage or theft; crew safe.
Armed robbery (offshore) — Four armed robbers boarded an offshore supply vessel near FPSO Miamte (~5 NM NE of Sanchez Magallanes) and stole crew belongings and property incl. SCBA sets.

CARB fuel & MISP — Only low-sulphur distillate (S<0.1%) accepted; EGCS/scrubber compliance not allowed (CARB Marine Notice 2020-1). Register at misp.io for annual & ballast reports; Biofouling Management Plan updated and paint certificate onboard for Marine Invasive Species inspection.

Expansion of emission control requirements — From 01 Jan 2025 CARB at-berth controls extend to ro-ro at all regulated terminals and tankers at LA/Long Beach; connect to OPS or use CARB-approved CAECS.
Customs fines — Strict customs rules; heavy fines for incomplete/inaccurate/undeclared items. Extra attention to paints/chemicals, bunkers/oils, electronics, tobacco/alcohol, engine/deck spares.
Customs fines — Strict review of customs declarations and store lists with penalties for inconsistencies; be attentive declaring paints/chemicals, bunkers/oils, electronics, tobacco/alcohol, spares.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — OOW sighted an individual entering bosun's store on a tanker; alarm raised, crew mustered, perpetrator absconded; nothing stolen. Port authorities notified.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Two robbers boarded a chemical tanker; spotted on port-side main deck. Escaped onto a waiting boat with unsecured items.
Whale strike reporting & safe distances — Humpback migration (Jun-Nov) raises collision risk. Maintain 100m either side / 300m front-behind; report to Ashburton VTS and authorities (DBCA, DCCEEW).

Requirements for LNG/alternate/dual-fuel vessels — First-time callers must comply and report in advance; in port Main Engine switch to LSFO/MGO before entering; aux/boiler only if instantly switchable.

Biofouling (CRMS) & entry — Clean hull required per Craft Risk Management Standard; follow MPI 5 steps (inspection, reports, paperwork, delay notice, pre-departure advice). Poor Knights Islands exclusion zone must be avoided (MSA fine). All seafarers require valid AU/NZ visas.
Biosecurity pre-arrival report (biofouling) — Ships must meet Craft Risk Management Standard (clean hull). Short stays (<=28d) allow light fouling; submit biofouling report with photos/video to MPI.

Flighted Spongy Moth Complex (FSMC) — FSMC (Lymantria dispar asiatica/japonica, L. umbrosa, L. postalba, L. albescens) native to China, Far-East Russia, Japan, Korea. Vessels calling East Asia/Russian Far East May-Oct must be certified free.

Flighted Spongy Moth Complex (FSMC) — FSMC moths (native China, Far-East Russia, Japan, Korea) lay tough eggs on ships near FSMC ports. Vessels calling East Asia/Russian Far East May-Oct must be certified free.

Biosecurity incident (live snails) — Live snails (treatment-resistant pest) found on a car deck; cargo ops suspended, vessel to anchorage; after three failed inspections lost berthing queue (>=8 days delay).

Garbage disposal restrictions & cost advisory — Strict biosecurity for garbage; food-contaminated items classified Biowaste and cannot be discharged; improper sorting may reject whole parcel. Disposal ~USD 4,000.
COFR bridging letter — For Brunswick, New York and US East Coast calls a bridging letter is required; verify COFR at npfc.uscg.mil/cofr. Georgia whale-speed reporting also applies (1 May - 15 Dec).

Penalty for garbage violation — A vessel fined when CBP found food waste (chicken bones, orange peels) mixed with general waste in cargo-deck bins from a previous port. Increase checks of garbage areas.
Fishery farms along China coast — Limited safe anchoring at Tianjin (esp. Dagukou North Anchorage); anchoring east risks entering fishery farms.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — Two robbers with knives seen in engine room of an anchored bulk carrier; escaped with engine spares on alarm.
New territorial sea baseline declaration — China revised baselines referenced for MARPOL actions (oil, sewage, garbage) in Beibu Gulf; non-compliance leads to heavy fines.
Guidance for bunkering in anchorages — Zhoushan guide for bunkering at Xiazhimen North, Tiaozhoumen, Xiushan East, Mazhi and Qushan Temporary anchorages.
New recommended passage — From 01 Jul 2024 0100 UTC new safety measures for vessels entering/exiting Kurushima Kaikyo Route; keep extra lookout and VHF watch.
Ballast water discharge fines — Guinea ratified MARPOL; Conakry prohibits discharge of harmful substances incl. ballast water; fines without Harbour Master permission.
Robbery (berth) — Three robbers with knives entered engine room, tied up duty crew, stole engine spares and released crew before escaping.
Robbery (anchorage) — Four robbers boarded a chemical tanker via anchor chain, broke into forecastle store and escaped with ship's stores.
Safety measures during fishing season — From 06 Jun 2024 (except Wed/Sun), 30 min before sunrise to ~1100 JST vessels not to enter traffic route; escort tug if transiting within hours.
Robbery (anchorage) — Five robbers boarded an anchored container ship and stole ship's property (fire nozzles, brass nuts/bolts, wire, portable fan).
Criminal attempt boarding — Crew on two tankers in transit each spotted four unauthorized individuals (one with a knife); alarm raised, perpetrators fled.
Robbery (anchorage) — Three robbers with guns and knives boarded an anchored bulk carrier, pointed guns at mustered crew and loaded ship stores into a waiting boat.
Stink bug (BMSB) season — Brown Marmorated Stink Bug, a hitchhiker pest, spreads via ocean-going vessels seeking winter shelter in containers/vehicles/machinery.
Stowaway — After departure a stowaway (claimed Tanzanian, ~39) was found on a car carrier; boarded via headline and hid in the starboard chain locker.
Crew abduction threat downgraded — Philippine operations dismantled Abu Sayyaf support base; PCG downgraded 'abduction for ransom' threat from MODERATE to MODERATE LOW.
Robbery / theft (underway) — Scrap metal taken from a towing barge by perpetrators in a small boat ~2.2 NM south of Pulau Mungging (Johor port limit).

Robbery / attempted robbery x2 — Incident 1: five perpetrators (one suspected firearm, one knife) in steering room (EB), nothing stolen. Incident 2: seven perpetrators ~4 NM NW of Pulau Cula; engine spares stolen.
Suspicious craft (USV) — An Unmanned Surface Vehicle approached a crude oil tanker ~48 NM SE of Mokha. Vessels near Yemen to increase watch and maintain sharp lookout.
Attempted robbery (berth) — Four perpetrators in a canoe approached a berthed offshore supply vessel; two boarded, spotted by duty crew, fled without stealing.
Attempted armed robbery — One perpetrator on the forecastle deck of a tanker pointed a handgun at crew and escaped. Ship's property stolen; coast guard/police searched.
Blockage of seawater strainers — Main-engine slowdowns from seawater strainers blocked by mass crustacean spawning in Western Anchorages. Inspect/clear before inbound pilotage.
Armed robbery (anchorage) — Four perpetrators with knives boarded an anchored bulk carrier; discovered on poop deck, escaped empty-handed on alarm.
Stowaway fines — GPHA USD 5,000 + Immigration USD 5,000 per stowaway (up to USD 10,000), excluding disembarkation/repatriation. Maintain gangway watch and pre-departure searches.
Maritime drug trafficking — Rise in smuggling targeting vessels in North/NE Brazil; pre-arrival seals, anchorage watch/lighting/CCTV, pre-departure void-space/underwater searches, sniffer dogs.
Robbery — Eight robbers with knives/steel bars boarded via hooks, overpowered/tied a crewman, broke into forecastle/paint lockers; escaped with ship property/stores.
CCTV onboard ships calling Indian ports — DGS circular (12 Feb 2025) mandates CCTV on certain vessels within 36 months (by 12 Feb 2028); Indian-flagged & SPL foreign-flagged mandatory.
Mooring line failures (expansion & weather) — Five mooring-line failures in six months linked to terminal expansion and severe cold fronts (Sep-Apr); no rope rental - arrive with sufficient lines.
Suspicious approach — A ~4m motorboat with 3 persons approached the stern of a bulk carrier underway; armed security fired warning shots, craft retreated.
Kidnapping — Ten pirates in one speedboat boarded a tanker SE of Santo Antonio; shots fired, crew in citadel. Pirates disembarked with ten kidnapped crew incl. Captain and Chief Engineer.
Unauthorized boarding — Eight perpetrators in two speedboats boarded a container ship NW of Santa Marta; crew in citadel, vessel diverted to Santa Marta. Crew safe, nothing stolen.
Monsoon preparedness — DG Shipping guidelines: strong tides, winds up to 45 km/h, heavy rain, zero visibility. Standby tugs, extra ropes. Foul-weather season 25 May-31 Aug; anchorage restricted.
Ballast water exchange requirements — Request de-ballasting permission >=72h before arrival; BWE in South China Sea/Pacific not accepted; ballast aged >=30 days not permitted; bottom outlets only.
Robbery — Four robbers boarded a product tanker underway SW of Brass; crew in citadel 4 hours. Crew belongings, cash, ship property stolen.
Suspicious approach — Four perpetrators on a motorboat approached a bulk carrier ~37 NM off Libreville; armed security fired warning shots, boat departed.
Robbery — A perpetrator boarded a product tanker in Monrovia anchorage; spotted on poop deck, escaped. Nothing stolen; reported to Monrovia RCC.
Robbery (anchorage) — Eight robbers with knives boarded a tanker at Beira; escaped on alarm. Stolen property later recovered by police.
World map confiscation by immigration — Chinese Immigration removed/destroyed a mess-room world map depicting Taiwan as independent. Review maps/publications for geopolitical compliance.

Ship pollution prevention regulations — Shanghai & Jiangsu regulations enforced on Yangtze ports (Taicang, Changshu, Nantong, Zhangjiagang, Jiangyin, Nanjing); penalties for untreated sewage; PSC detention risk.

Enforcement against anchoring outside zones — Strict anchoring rules near southern entrance of Istanbul Strait (Ambarli PA); anchoring outside zones may trigger escort tugs, underwater inspections and fines.
Port situation & safe navigation — Libyan ports normal; coastal area Benghazi-Derna restricted - no entry. Vessels inside fined >= LD 250,000 (~USD 50,000). Stay >=40 miles away.
Robbery (anchorage) — Two robbers boarded a container vessel; spotted near forecastle, escaped down a rope. Fire nozzles, hydrant caps, hoses, deck air-valve caps stolen.
Armed robbery (offshore) — Five perpetrators boarded a vessel offshore Kakinada from a fishing boat; Coast Guard detained them after a short pursuit.

Warning against soot blowing alongside — Port warns against soot blowing and unmaintained spark arrestors; non-compliant vessels removed from berth, flagged for stricter vetting. Comply with SMS/ISGOTT.
Increased vigilance vs unauthorized activities — MMEA/MMD require official approval before any activity in Malaysian waters (incl. EEZ) and anchoring only in designated areas. Keep AIS on.

Flighted Spongy Moth Complex outbreak — FSMC outbreak in Hokkaido (Jul-Aug). Vessels may carry sticky egg masses on hulls, risking delays/costs at quarantine in US, Canada, NZ, Chile, Argentina, Australia.
Criminal boarding — A container vessel boarded SSW of Lagos; two crew briefly held, freed after Portuguese Navy response. Framing points to organized narcotrafficking, not piracy.
Stowaway detection — Vessel berthed/discharged with gangway watch; two suspected stowaways detected underway. Returned to Djibouti; no contraband; handed to police.
Robbery / armed robbery (platform) — Robbers with rifles boarded an oil platform NW of Ciudad del Carmen, fired into air, stole self-contained breathing apparatus and fled.
Robbery / armed robbery (OSV) — Six robbers with pistols/rifles boarded an offshore supply vessel off Dos Bocas, threatened crew, stole breathing apparatuses and escaped.

New requirements for vessels with China/HK/Macau links — From 31 Mar 2025 Taiwan enforces national security reviews for vessels linked to Mainland China/HK/Macau; applies to 'black flag' registries and certain ship types.
Robbery (anchorage) — Three perpetrators boarded a tanker at Balongan, stole ship stores and escaped. No injuries.
Attempted robbery (anchorage) — One robber on the port-side main deck of a tanker jumped overboard when spotted and escaped with an accomplice. Nothing stolen.
Suspicious approach — Two skiffs with 6-7 persons approached a vessel at Tema; crew employed BMP. Incident lasted 25 min, no harm. Assessed as suspicious approach.

Prohibition of Starlink in Chinese waters/ports — Starlink not permitted in Chinese waters/ports; authorities boarded a vessel at Nansha reminding it stay off. Turn off before entering Chinese limits.

Steps against maritime drug trafficking — Rise in rip-on/rip-off smuggling. Prior arrival: brief crew, review security plan/CCTV/lighting/access. In port: strict gangway control, patrols, recheck seals.
Public health measures (dengue) — Due to dengue in the Caribbean (esp. Haiti, Cuba), DR increased public-health vigilance per IHR 2005; expect vector-control inspections, breeding-site checks.

Attempted boarding — A tanker approached by a wooden boat with three persons in lifejackets speaking aggressively over VHF; security procedures for two hours; Benin Navy dispatched. Likely local fishermen.
Armed boarding (piracy) — A tanker under attack SE of Hobyo; one craft with armed perpetrators fired small arms and RPGs and boarded the vessel.

Crude oil washing (COW) operations administration — From 01 Jan 2026 ships doing COW in Shanghai MSA waters need certified COW & inert gas systems, calibrated gas detectors, approved COW Manual, trained crew; report 12h before; strict O2 limits.
Brown Marmorated Stink Bug (BMSB) season — BAF BMSB risk season started. High-risk: China & Korea (heightened surveillance only); Canada, Japan, Taiwan, USA, Italy (mandatory treatment).

Customs experience exchange — At Lima/Delta Dock Customs found 7 bullet-proof jackets and 8 helmets in a security locker not declared and demanded USD 7,000 without receipt; Master refused, demand withdrawn.

Armed robbery x2 — Two incidents on anchored container ships; perpetrators (>2 each) broke forecastle-store security; small portable items (20L paint drums, hydrant caps, electrical cord coil) stolen.
Breach of local hot work rule — A vessel under PSC at Taicang detained for 4 deficiencies (3 detainable); departure delayed because welding done without prior Port MSA Hot Work Permit.
Kinetic attack — A tanker hit by two unconfirmed projectiles in Port of Bahrain, causing an engine-room fire (later controlled); crew evacuated. Also hit by an uncrewed surface vehicle (USV).
Kinetic attack — A vessel hit by fallen debris from an intercepted vessel at Ras Laffan; bridge window damaged. Crew safe.
Attempted boarding — Several perpetrators attempted to board a containership at San Pedro anchorage; alarm raised, perpetrators fled in a wooden boat.
UAV attack — A UAV attack on Novorossiysk caused a fire at the oil depot; drone fragments landed at the fuel terminal, injuring two people.
TWIC shore access — Shore leave requires TWIC compliance; obtain arrangements from local agent, especially at Charleston. Crew must confirm with Master before going ashore.
COFR bridging letter — Bridging letter required for New York / East Coast calls; check COFR status at npfc.uscg.mil/cofr before arrival.
Whale speed limit (TSS) — Voluntary participation in San Francisco TSS whale speed restrictions; feed into passage plan and comply during 1 May - 15 Dec.
1-Call Alaska & Aleutian ATBA — Notify the 1-Call Alaska provider when transiting; IMO Aleutian Areas To Be Avoided marked on ECDIS, inform 1-Call if entry needed.
IMO Area To Be Avoided off the Washington Coast — reflect in passage plan and keep clear.
Oil-spill response agreements — WCMRC (West) / ECRC (East) agreements required for Canadian calls incl. New Westminster and Tacoma; ERTV & Juan de Fuca Agreement applicable.

Whale slowdown & navigation limits — Voluntary slowdown at Swiftsure Bank (Jun-Oct) and Haro Strait/Boundary Pass (Jun-Nov), No-Go Zone at San Juan Island. Canada is an AGM country. Check H&M navigation limits and SSMM 7.33 ice/cold-weather precautions.
Terminal access — Walking or cycling inside Zeebrugge terminal is prohibited; crew must contact the agency for arranged transport to/from the gate.
HIT berth access — At Humber International Terminal the ship's ramp/gangway may become unusable at low tide; arrange the shore gangway via local agent or HIT to keep safe access.

Shore access & heaving lines — Crew walking to town must use designated walkways wearing Hi-Viz vests. Monkey fist must be <500 g without added weights (penalties imposed at Southampton and Amsterdam).
Compulsory garbage/sludge collection — Per EU directive a constant collection fee for garbage and sludge/bilge applies to all vessels calling Piraeus; discharge per port regulation.

KIA Terminal / PIRT — Transshipment of unlashed vehicles between KIA Terminal & PIRT per WW instruction INF-12-23. KIA Terminal prohibits shore vehicles >7 t (affects lube-oil supply; plan LO stems in advance).

Fishing nets & territorial sea — Check set-nets on the route with local agent before arrival. Foreign ships must not navigate Japanese territorial sea (3NM) / internal waters with restricted actions except emergencies.

Mooring & pilot boarding — Mooring winch brake rendering test at intervals not exceeding 24 months (rules effective 1 Feb 2023). Strict pilot boarding arrangement: photos submitted with 48h NOA; non-compliance cancels the schedule until rectification.
Expanded VTS area — Port of Melbourne VTS area expanded (Victorian NtM 127/2023); comply with VTS reporting and general traffic procedures.

Reef navigation & Queensland pilotage — Penalties imposed for improper navigation in the Great Barrier Reef. Queensland pilotage: EPL/ShaPoLi must be immediately overridable; fuel changeover completed and propulsion tested 2h before pilot boarding (30 min from berth); no changeover under pilotage.
Pilot boarding safety — Ports of Auckland safety update: risk of improperly secured pilot ladders; verify rigging and securing before pilot transfer.

Stowaway regulation — Stowaways boarding at Durban will not be landed back: if deemed stowaways they sail with the vessel to the next port. Heightened stowaway watch and pre-departure searches required.
Blue-whale routing (WalWil fleet) — Company TSS moved ~15NM south of the current TSS to avoid whale feeding grounds: westbound 05 30N-05 35N, eastbound 05 24N-05 29N. Reflect in passage plan.
